newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish O/N at lombard on reserve-end, zloty down.
newsitem.headline: Polish O/N at lombard on reserve-end, zloty down.

text.p: Polish O/N rates at the lombard rate of 25 percent as the market tightened on the last working day of the March reserve period and on cash withdrawals before Easter holidays, dealers said.

They said, however, tomorrow/next rates eased two points below the lombard rate signalling the market may regain liquidity next week and rates were expected to trade around 23 percent at the start of the April reserve period on Tuesday.
"The market lifted overnight rates to the lombard rate, but the situation should improve next week, as T/N depos are traded lower," said Ewa Sokolowska from Kredyt Bank SA.

At 0845 GMT overnight deposit rates were quoted at 24.70/25.05 percent against 24.85/25.20 percent at opening and tomorrow/next rates were at 23.00/23.60 percent against the opening's 22.70/25.20 percent.

Dealers said some smaller banks might have problems with taking lombard financing because their treasuries portfolios, used as collateral for the lombard credit, were often scattered in repo transactions with clients.
They said clients were likely to gain the most on the current market tightness placing surpluses with banks at higher rates.
"Today I had to accept a six-day client's deposit at 23 percent, while normally I would pay some 20.5 percent," a dealer at a Polish bank said.
The zloty weakened against the parity rate on small importers' orders amid slow trade with European markets closed for Good Friday.

At 0910 GMT the zloty was quoted at 2.95/2.85 percent from the trading band centre, down from 2.97/2.88 percent at opening. It was at 3.0730/60 to the dollar, down from 3.0720/50 at opening and at 1.8335/55 to the mark against 1.8335/50.
